sections.h2: Where is the Durham County Register of Deeds and when can I record a deed?
sections.html:
The office is on the second floor of Durham County Administration Building II, 201 East Main Street, Durham, NC 27701. The county's Real Estate Records page lists recording hours as Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:45pm, except holidays, and the main line is 919-560-0480.

Durham County held about 347,240 people on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, packed into 286.53 square miles of land. Most sellers never walk into the counter. The closing attorney or title company submits the deed, and the register of deeds stamps it, indexes it and returns it. What you control is the paperwork that goes in, so it helps to know what the office will and will not accept.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Durham County?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page after that, according to the county's posted fee schedule. Mortgages and deeds of trust follow a separate line, and a satisfaction of a mortgage costs nothing to record.

Durham County recording fees as the county fee schedule prints them (source: dconc.gov Register of Deeds Fee Schedule)
ItemFee printed by the county
Instruments except deeds of trust and mortgages$26.00 first 15 pages / $4 each add'l page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00 first 35 pages / $4 each add'l page
Plats$21.00 each sheet
Nonstandard document$25.00
Multiple instruments as one, each$10.00
Satisfaction instrumentsNo Fee
Additional subsequent instrument index reference, each$10.00
Certified copies$5.00 first page, $2 each add'l page

These amounts come from the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, which treats the listed fees as complete and exclusive and has the office collect them before filing.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on a Durham County sale?
sections.html:
North Carolina charges one dollar on each $500 of the price or value, rounded up for any fraction of $500, and the seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed can be recorded. The rule sits in G.S. 105-228.30.

The register of deeds splits what it collects. One half goes to the county general fund, and the other half is remitted to the state each month, with the county allowed to keep 2% of the state's share. Your closing statement will show the figure, so ask the settlement agent to confirm the line before you sign.

  • The tax is tied to the consideration or value of the interest conveyed, as the statute words it.
  • The seller is the party who owes it, which matters when you compare a cash offer against a listing.
  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust carry no recording fee, so a payoff at closing adds no cost at the counter.

sections.h2: Can I record a deed electronically in Durham County?
sections.html:
Yes. The office takes electronic submissions through approved vendors, and a document received by 4:45 pm is processed and returned the same business day. The county lists four vendors for anyone who wants an account.

  • Corporation Service Company (CSC)
  • eRecording Partners Network, LLC (ePN)
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile

Title companies already hold these accounts, which is why a Durham closing can finish in a single day. A private seller who signs a deed outside a closing would contact one of the vendors directly or deliver the original during the posted hours.

sections.h2: What format does a Durham County deed need to follow?
sections.html:
The deed has to meet the layout rules in G.S. 161-14(b), and the county posts them on its Document Recording Standards page. A paper that misses a rule is still recorded, but the office adds a $25.00 nonstandard fee on top of the usual charges.

  • Page size of 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14, typed on white paper.
  • A 3 inch blank margin at the top of the first page and a half inch margin on the other sides of that page and on every side of later pages.
  • Text no smaller than 9 points, printed on one side only. Blanks and corrections may be filled in by pen.
  • The type of instrument stated at the top of the first page.
  • Plat maps cut to 18 by 24.

If the only defect is print smaller than 9 points, the registrar may record the instrument without the nonstandard fee when it is legible.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter when I sell my Durham County house?
sections.html:
Recording sets the order of claims on the land. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not protect the buyer against lien creditors or other purchasers who paid value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the time of registration.

The register of deeds records what it is handed and has no authority to fix errors on a recorded instrument. The county's standards page says that includes misspelled names, a defective legal description or a wrong parcel number. A person who spots an indexing mistake emails the office, and it records an Administrative Notice linked to the original entry. Proofread the deed before it leaves the closing table.

Owners can also sign up for the Recording Notification Service, which emails an alert whenever a document is recorded under their name. That is a quick way to catch a fraudulent filing against a vacant or inherited house.

sections.h2: How do property taxes affect recording a deed in Durham County?
sections.html:
The register of deeds does not collect property tax. Durham County Tax Administration lists, assesses and collects it, and the county reappraised all real property effective January 1, 2025. Their office is at 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, with a main number of 919-560-0300.

The tax office states that the bill is sent to the owner of record as of January 1 and that a former owner should pass it on to the buyer. If you sell mid-year, ask the tax collector for the amount outstanding before closing so the settlement agent can settle it. The Durham property tax guide on this site walks through the dates and relief programs.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Durham County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for Durham County gives a picture of the market the recording office serves.

  • Housing units: 164,222 in July 2025, with 141,847 households counted for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 55.5%, with a median owner-occupied value of $389,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,508. Median household income: $82,316.
  • Building permits in 2025: 4,772.
  • Population change from the April 2020 estimates base to July 2025: 6.9%.

Because the transfer tax follows the price, a higher median value here means a larger tax line on the closing statement, so compare any offer against net proceeds line by line.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Durham County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. State law makes the transferor responsible for paying the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate is one dollar for each $500 of consideration or fraction of $500, and the county and the state each receive half.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage payoff in Durham County?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee schedule lists satisfaction instruments at no fee, so releasing a deed of trust at closing does not add a recording charge.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed uses small print?
faqs.a: The office can record it. A document that misses the layout rules is accepted after the $25.00 nonstandard fee, and the registrar may waive that fee when the only problem is print under 9 points and the page is still legible.

faqs.q: Can I send a deed to the Durham County Register of Deeds by e-recording myself?
faqs.a: Individuals normally go through a vendor. The county names CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile, and each vendor sets up the account. Documents received by 4:45 pm come back the same business day.

faqs.q: Who fixes a misspelled name on a recorded Durham County deed?
faqs.a: The register of deeds cannot change it. The office records and indexes documents as presented, so ask the closing attorney how to fix an error in the deed itself. An indexing mistake can be reported by email, and the office then records an Administrative Notice referencing the original entry.
